clue.text: Striking 'type of art associated with the RA

definitions.meaning: vivid and arresting, as a striking entrance is

definitions.text: type of art associated with the RA
definitions.meaning: the Royal Academy of ... Art (RADA) teaches the art of the stage, so this is the kind of art named in its title

explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, the London drama school; 'the RA' points at the first two letters of its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking gesture is theatrical and eye-catching; the second sense is the adjective in the drama school's name.

clue.text: In the old party there's nothing to extirpate

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed inside the word for the old party

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a large evening party or assembly
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the bygone political party there is nothing left to wipe out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old party' tempts toward TORY or WHIG; it is ROUT, an archaic word for a fashionable gathering, split RO...UT around O and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To extirpate is to destroy completely, to pull up weeds by the roots.

clue.text: Russian capitalist?

definitions.meaning: with the question mark, one who lives in a capital city rather than a financier

explanation.definitionFit: A native of Moscow is both a Russian and, punningly, a dweller in the Russian capital.

clue.text: Twist's moment to speak might one say?

indicators.note: the question marks that the word for speaking is said out loud, giving a matching sound

parts.note: to talk is to speak

explanation.surface: A question about when a dance called the twist gets its chance to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same, with no R heard.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics the turning effect of a force, its moment, is what makes something twist.

clue.text: Putting on the yellow seemingly with this handicap

definitions.text: Putting on the yellow seemingly with this handicap

parts.words: Putting on the yellow seemingly with this handicap
parts.note: someone unable to tell hues apart might wear yellow while believing it is another shade

explanation.surface: Someone dressing in yellow because of a disability.
explanation.definitionFit: This condition stops a person telling certain hues apart, so the yellow garment was only 'seemingly' chosen.

clue.text: Regimental Goat for first of May race-meeting

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the month's name is wanted

parts.note: Royal Ascot is a famous horse-race meeting in Berkshire, England

explanation.surface: A regiment's goat entered for an early-summer race day.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the English racecourse whose Royal meeting is a June society event. Some British regiments, such as the Royal Welsh, keep a goat as their regimental animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Several British regiments parade a goat as their lucky emblem animal.

clue.text: New chance I'm giving him, a garage job

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man is given a second chance, a job at a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges CHANCE IM; 'him, a garage job' defines the person by his work.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who repairs cars in a garage is this tradesman.

clue.text: Gilpin was one of credit and renown

definitions.text: Gilpin was one of credit and renown

parts.words: Gilpin was one of credit and renown
parts.note: quotes Cowper's comic ballad John Gilpin, whose hero is introduced as a London townsman of credit and renown

explanation.surface: A man called Gilpin was well thought of and famous.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cowper's poem opens: 'John Gilpin was a citizen / Of credit and renown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper's line describes the draper as a respected townsman of London, the word the poem uses.

clue.text: Passing where a pole is set up in the river

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
N, the north pole

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is is written upwards, reading backwards

explanation.surface: Describing a place where someone has driven a pole upright into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns IS into SI, so A, N and SI make ANSI, which sits inside TRENT, an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing lasts only a short while, fleeting and temporary.

clue.text: Tom who day-dreams about love

indicators.note: the dreamer's word goes round the letter for love

parts.note: a muser is one who ponders or day-dreams
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A man called Tom who daydreams about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, not a man's name here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat that catches mice earns this name.

clue.text: Sordid gain by Spanish aunt or Roman matron

parts.note: filthy lucre is money got dishonourably
tia is Spanish for aunt

explanation.surface: Dirty money, a Spanish aunt, or a woman of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend she was a virtuous Roman wife whose rape by Tarquin led to the fall of Rome's kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary wife of Collatinus is the model virtuous married woman of early Roman history.

clue.text: 50th of US capital growth in post-war period

definitions.text: 50th of US capital growth in post-war period

parts.words: 50th of US capital growth in post-war period
parts.note: the capital of the fiftieth American state, admitted in 1959, whose rise came after the Second World War

explanation.surface: A statistic about investment returns in the years after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's '50c.' is 50th: Hawaii became the fiftieth state in 1959, so its capital joined the list of US state capitals in the post-war years.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii, the last state admitted, has this city on Oahu as its seat of government.

clue.text: Stuns tough female, on coming off at point-to-point

indicators.note: the word on is taken away from the warrior woman

parts.note: an Amazon is a strong warrior woman
taken as written
E and S, east and south, two compass points side by side

explanation.surface: A hardy woman amazes onlookers by falling off at a point-to-point horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase meeting in Britain; here it is two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to leave them stunned.

clue.text: One of a number in flight in this case

definitions.text: One of a number in flight in this case

parts.words: One of a number in flight in this case
parts.note: a flight is a set of steps, and 'this case' adds the word for the enclosing structure

explanation.surface: A bird in a flock, in this instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Add 'case' to the answer and you get the structure housing the flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one of the many in a flight of steps.

clue.text: Jack seen in tenuous sunshine by night?.

indicators.note: the sailor appears within the word for tenuous

parts.note: slight means flimsy or tenuous
a jack tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A man glimpsed in weak sunlight after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars are suns, so their light is sunshine at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The stars are distant suns, so the glow they give after dark is a kind of night-time sunshine.

clue.text: 'e follows one basic contortion with a bow

indicators.note: the words are twisted out of shape into a new order

parts.note: 'e is a dropped-aitch he, leaving just the letter

explanation.surface: Cockney 'e copies a simple twisting movement and then bows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts E after OBEISANC, the anagram of ONE BASIC from 'contortion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep bow is a gesture of respect or homage.

clue.text: Place advertisement about ring one left behind

indicators.note: the short advertisement goes round the following pieces

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
a band is a ring, as a wedding band
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to put a notice in the paper about a lost ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' is just the instruction to set AD around BAND and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserted or left behind has been given up.

clue.text: Cause of painful sunburn for a swimmer.?

definitions.meaning: split in two, a sting from a ray of sunlight is what burns
a flat sea fish with a venomous tail

explanation.definitionFit: Split as sting plus ray it is a burning sunbeam; whole, it is a venomous flat fish of warm seas.

clue.text: Bound to follow a direction to find out

indicators.note: the word for bound comes after the other pieces

parts.note: S for south, a compass direction
bound, as in bound to win, means certain

explanation.surface: Someone obliged to obey an instruction in order to discover something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' is the adjective, as in 'bound to happen', not a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain a fact is to establish or discover it for sure.

clue.text: Prometheus thus bound can hide if set free:

indicators.note: the letters are freed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Titan tied to a rock could hide if only he were released.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Prometheus was fastened to a rock as punishment for giving fire to humans.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus had the Titan fastened with fetters to a rock, so he was held fast.

clue.text: Vocally refuse to give body measurement

indicators.note: the word for refuse is spoken, giving a matching sound

parts.note: waste is rubbish, refuse as a noun

explanation.surface: Someone verbally declining to give their measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like the verb to decline; it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor measures round the middle of the torso for trousers.

clue.text: In Xanadu Alph ran "down to a ---- sea"

definitions.text: In Xanadu Alph ran "down to a ---- sea"

parts.words: In Xanadu Alph ran "down to a ---- sea"
parts.note: fill the gap in Coleridge's Kubla Khan, where the sacred river runs through caverns to a dark sea

explanation.surface: A line from a poem with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Kubla Khan: 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran / Through caverns measureless to man / Down to a sunless sea.'
explanation.definitionFit: The missing poetic word describes a sea deep underground where daylight never reaches.

clue.text: Plant article about an intelligence agency

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
ca, short for circa, means about
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: A news article about a spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could suggest a spy, fitting the surface, but it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The wattle or thorn tree of Africa and Australia is this plant.

clue.text: What a baker had 'to depart north to get?

parts.note: to leave is to depart
N is north

explanation.surface: What a baker needed to go north for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had to depart' reads as one obligation; the definition stops at 'had'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers use yeast or another raising agent to make dough rise.

clue.text: Like a roue not disheartened after ten years

indicators.note: the trimmed word comes after the ten-year span

parts.note: a decade is ten years

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letter, is taken out of the word not

explanation.surface: A rake still in good spirits after a decade.
explanation.walkthrough: A roue is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake given to debauchery is self-indulgent and morally declining.

clue.text: Ed: German perhaps, or Bobby French

indicators.note: the letters might perhaps be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A man called Ed, maybe German, or a French one named Bobby.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British policeman; read 'Bobby French' as 'a French bobby'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French police officer is the counterpart of a British bobby.

clue.text: Many a girl's choice of Riviera resort

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
Anne's, a girl's name with possessive s

explanation.surface: A popular holiday spot on the French coast that many young women pick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many a girl's' reads as one phrase but splits into C and ANNE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: This town on the Mediterranean coast of France hosts a famous film festival.

clue.text: Having had double liqueur starters taken in neat

indicators.note: the opening letters are taken into the word for neat

parts.note: tidy means neat

indicators.note: the first letter of each word is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone who downed a large liqueur straight, without mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having had' is short for having had a drink or two; 'neat' looks like undiluted spirit but means tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has had a few drinks is tipsy, slightly drunk.

clue.text: Blow and bother! That's careless

parts.note: a slap is a blow
dash it! is a mild oath, like bother!

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation at someone's sloppiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash!' is a dated British exclamation of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done hastily and carelessly is sloppy.
